name: Southern Pied-Babbler
rangeDescription: Namibia to botswana, western zimbabwe, and northwestern south africa
description: A striking black-and-white babbler lacking any facial markings. Groups of 3-15 range through arid savanna, preferring areas with thorn trees, where they associate with Red-billed Buffalo-Weaver and Crimson-breasted Gonolek.

name: Chuuk Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Chuuk (western caroline islands)
description: A species of forest and forest edge habitats on Micronesia’s Chuuk Islands. Combination of bluish-gray head, pale orange throat and breast, brown-tinged wings, and slightly peaked head is unique on the islands.

name: Ashy-headed Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southwestern sri lanka
description: Medium-sized, rufous babbler with a gray hood, beady pale eye, buff throat patch, and blackish bill and legs. Gregarious, usually encountered within small groups low in the understory, or on the ground, in wet forests of the lowlands and foothills.

name: Rufous-necked Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Mixed forest of eastern nepal to southwestern china, northeastern india, and myanmar
description: This laughingthrush’s color palette is simple but smooth and unique: dark gray overall with a black face and pumpkin-orange neck and vent. Favors forest edge and scrubby habitat more than most other laughingthrushes in its range; also often found along rivers and in reedbeds.

name: Western Kingbird
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters southern mexico to costa rica and (?) panama
description: Fairly large yellow-bellied flycatcher; common and widespread in western North America. Rather pale gray head with weakly contrasting whitish throat and breast, and lemon-yellow belly.

name: Standard-winged Nightjar
rangeDescription: In breeding season from senegambia to liberia, eastward to southwestern south sudan, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern uganda (present during the season in southern portion of this region, but breeding there not confirmed); winters north and east from southern mauritania and northern sengeal eastward to central chad, southern sudan, eastern south sudan, central uganda, eritrea, western ethiopia, and western kenya
description: Females and non-breeding males are ordinary-looking, fairly plain nightjars, but breeding males have absurd “standards” growing out of the middle of their wings. In flight, they give the impression of a nightjar being chased by two bats.

name: Black-faced Solitaire
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama (east to veraguas)
description: Sleek medium-sized thrush with a beautiful voice. Listen for its fluty, ethereal phrases drifting over montane forests.

name: Chestnut-tipped Toucanet
rangeDescription: Far southern colombia along east slope of andes to bolivia
description: Small, green toucan found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes. Plumage is mostly green, but note white throat, chestnut tip to the tail, and mostly black bill with thin, white line at base.

name: Puerto Rican Lizard-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Puerto rico
description: An impressive long-tailed bird of wooded habitats including shade coffee plantations. Usually found in dense vegetation though sometimes found sunning in the open at first light with its tail spread.

name: Gray Pratincole
rangeDescription: Rivers of mali to cameroon, western democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern angola
description: A compact, elegant pratincole, mostly pale gray above with a warm buffy nape that sometimes extends to the breast and a striking black-and-white face pattern; the legs and base of the bill are reddish. In flight, the striking black-and-white patterning in the wings and tail is unique.

name: Javan Blue-banded Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Java
description: Very rare, small kingfisher of forested streams and rivers up to the lower mountains. Highly threatened and found at very few remaining sites.

name: Böhm's Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southeastern africa (malawi and adjacent countries)
description: Slim green bee-eater with an orange throat and crown, a black tip to the tail, and elongated black tail streamers. Found very locally in moist woodland and forest edge, usually near rivers and streams.

name: Black-faced Spoonbill
rangeDescription: Breeds northeastern china and korea; winters to southeastern asia
description: Large white waterbird with a long spatula-shaped bill. Breeding adults have long plumes on the head and a smudging of yellow on the chest.

name: Painted Stork
rangeDescription: Lowlands of indian subcontinent to southern china and southeastern asia
description: A large stork with a long yellow bill that curves down at the tip, like that of an Ibis. Adult is primarily white with black striped markings on the wings and bright pink on tertials.

name: Black-and-white Tanager
rangeDescription: Locally from western ecuador to northwestern peru; eastern peru to northwestern bolivia
description: Highly distinctive and unusual species that is more reminiscent of a large seedeater. It has a unique migration pattern, breeding during the rainy season in the Tumbes eco-region in northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador and wintering in the western Amazon.

name: Madagascar Buzzard
rangeDescription: Woodland and savanna of madagascar
description: Typical brown buzzard that is endemic to Madagascar. Found throughout the island in many different habitats, though absent from pure grassland.

name: Veracruz Wren
rangeDescription: Lowlands of central veracruz (eastern mexico)
description: Large wren occurring locally in a small area on the Gulf Coast of Veracruz. Usually found in small groups, less often in pairs.

name: Bornean Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed lowlands of borneo
description: Large, stout wren-babbler. Highly dependent on pristine lowland forests; populations now declining and increasingly fragmented across Borneo as that habitat is rapidly deforested.

name: Screaming Piha
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, northern bolivia, and amazonian and eastern brazil
description: One of the most characteristic sounds of Amazonian lowlands. This drab gray cotinga is commonly heard but infrequently seen throughout its range.

name: Tongan Megapode
rangeDescription: Forest of niuafo'ou (northwestern tonga); recently introduced to late and fonualei, and populations formerly on other tongan islands have died out
description: A plump, mostly ground-dwelling bird with long yellowish legs and a dark gray body with slightly browner wash on the wings and back. Head mostly dark gray, with bright orange beak and whitish crest.
